content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Use Punnett squares to predict offspring ratios
Calculate probability of offspring genotypes and phenotypes
Interpret the results of genetic crosses

is the inheritance of a single characteristic controlled by one gene with two alleles. Understanding monohybrid inheritance allows us to predict the likely outcomes of genetic crosses and understand how characteristics are passed from parents to offspring.
is a grid used to predict the possible offspring from a genetic cross.
How to draw a Punnett square:
Write the genotypes of both parents
Separate the alleles each parent can pass on (gametes)
Put one parent's alleles across the top
Put the other parent's alleles down the side
Fill in the boxes by combining alleles
TT can only produce T gametes
tt can only produce t gametes

content.text: Tt × Tt (both parents are tongue rollers but heterozygous)
Tt can produce T or t gametes
Tt can produce T or t gametes
3:1 ratio is characteristic of Tt × Tt crosses
- used to determine if an organism showing the dominant phenotype is homozygous or heterozygous.

From a Tt × Tt cross, what is the probability of a child being:
a) Homozygous dominant (TT)?
b) A tongue roller?
c) Not a tongue roller?

a) TT: 1 out of 4 = 1/4 = 25%
b) Tongue roller (TT or Tt): 3 out of 4 = 3/4 = 75%
c) Non-roller (tt): 1 out of 4 = 1/4 = 25%
Each fertilisation is an independent event.
If a couple who are both Tt have already had 3 children who are all tongue rollers, the probability that their next child will be a non-roller is still 1/4 (25%).
Previous offspring do not affect future probabilities.
is used to determine the genotype of an organism showing the dominant phenotype.
Cross the unknown individual with a homozygous recessive individual.
A brown mouse could be BB or Bb. Cross it with a white mouse (bb).
If all offspring are brown → parent was BB
If some offspring are white → parent was Bb

content.text: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant to short (t). Two tall pea plants are crossed. Some of the offspring are short.

a) What are the genotypes of the parents?
b) Draw a Punnett square for this cross.
c) What proportion of the offspring will be short?
a) Both parents must be heterozygous (Tt) because they produce short offspring (tt).
c) 1 out of 4 offspring will be short = 1/4 = 25%
Real-World Application: Inheritance of Cystic Fibrosis
Cystic fibrosis (CF) is caused by a recessive allele (f).
Ff = carrier (normal but carries CF allele)
A 3:1 ratio means exactly 3 dominant and 1 recessive offspring
3:1 is a probability ratio. With small numbers, actual ratios may vary due to chance.
Previous offspring affect the probability of the next one
Each fertilisation is independent. Having 3 boys doesn't mean the next child is more likely to be a girl.
All offspring from Tt × Tt will be in perfect 3:1 ratio
This is an expected ratio. Actual results may differ, especially with small sample sizes.
A child can only inherit alleles that the parents show in their phenotype
Heterozygous parents can pass on recessive alleles they don't express
Grid used to predict offspring genotypes
Sex cell containing one allele for each gene
Crossing with homozygous recessive to determine genotype
Monohybrid inheritance involves one gene with two alleles
Punnett squares predict possible offspring genotypes and phenotypes
Tt × Tt gives a 3:1 phenotype ratio (3 dominant : 1 recessive)
Tt × tt gives a 1:1 phenotype ratio
Each fertilisation is an independent event
Test crosses determine if an organism is homozygous or heterozygous
Probability can be expressed as fractions, percentages, or ratios
